slot.brief: Calorimetry with phase change: ice at 0°C added to warm water; find final temperature or mass of ice melted using latent heat and specific heat, comparing the heat lost and gained.

stem: In separate trials, excess ice at $0^\circ\text{C}$ is added to $100$ g of water at $40^\circ\text{C}$ and $150$ g of water at $20^\circ\text{C}$. What is the ratio of the masses of ice melted? Take $c_{\text{water}}=1$ cal g$^{-1}\,{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ and $L_f=80$ cal g$^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Ice melted = heat released by water ÷ L_f. The two trials melt 100×40/80 = 50 g and 150×20/80 = 37.5 g, respectively; ratio = 4:3.

working:
$Q_1=100(1)(40)=4000$ cal, $Q_2=150(1)(20)=3000$ cal
$m_1=Q_1/L_f=50$ g, $m_2=Q_2/L_f=37.5$ g
$m_1:m_2=50:37.5=4:3$

Independent check: Ice melted = heat released by water ÷ L_f. The two trials melt 100×40/80 = 50 g and 150×20/80 = 37.5 g, respectively; ratio = 4:3.
solution:
Heat released by the water melts the ice: $Q=mc_{\text{water}}\Delta T=m_{\text{ice}}L_f$.
$$m_1=\frac{100\times1\times40}{80}=50\text{ g},\qquad m_2=\frac{150\times1\times20}{80}=37.5\text{ g}$$
Thus, $m_1:m_2=50:37.5=4:3$.
